question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-3} & =5\cdot {8}^{2x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {8}^{2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x-3=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {8}^{2x}).
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{2x}) \\ x-3 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =3+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =3+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x & =\frac{3+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$
